keyPoints: Same shaded region proves set equality
Grouping does not change a chain of unions or of intersections
Check union and intersection laws separately
modelAnswer:
The shaded diagrams give identical regions on both sides in each case, so
$(A \cup B) \cup C=A \cup(B \cup C)$ and $(A \cap B) \cap C=A \cap(B \cap C)$.
Hence the associative laws of union and intersection are verified by diagrams.
stem: Verify associative law of union and intersection by using diagrams of question 1.

keyPoints: Union over intersection mirrors expansion of brackets
Intersection distributes over union symmetrically

modelAnswer:

(ii) Shading $A \cap(B \cup C)$ gives the same picture as shading $(A \cap B) \cup(A \cap C)$.
Both distributive properties are therefore verified by the diagrams.
stem:

keyPoints: Compute inner bracket first
Equal results on both sides verify the law
Empty intersections make both sides empty
modelAnswer:
(i) With $P=\{0,1,2,3\}$, $Q=\{2,3,4,5,6\}$, $R=\{5,6,7,8,9\}$:
(a) $(P \cup Q) \cup R=\{0,1,2,\ldots,9\}=P \cup(Q \cup R)$.
(b) $(P \cap Q) \cap R=\{2,3\} \cap\{5,6,7,8,9\}=\varnothing=P \cap(Q \cap R)$ since $Q \cap R=\{5,6\}$.
(ii) With $P=\{m,n,o,p,q\}$, $Q=\{r,s,t,u\}$, $R=\{t,u,v,w\}$:
(a) both groupings give $\{m,n,o,p,q,r,s,t,u,v,w\}$.
(b) $(P \cap Q) \cap R=\varnothing$ and $P \cap(Q \cap R)=P \cap\{t,u\}=\varnothing$.
Both associative laws hold in each case.
stem:

when

keyPoints: Check subset relationships before computing
$X \cup(Y \cap Z)=(X \cup Y) \cap(X \cup Z)$ is the distributive law
Subsets simplify unions and intersections at once
modelAnswer:
$X=\{-1,-2,-3\}$, $Y=\{0,1,2,3\}$, $Z=\{0,\pm1,\pm2,\pm3\}$.
Since $Y \subset Z$, we get $Y \cap Z=Y$.
Left side: $X \cup(Y \cap Z)=X \cup Y=\{-3,-2,-1,0,1,2,3\}$.
Right side: $(X \cup Y) \cap(X \cup Z)=\{-3,-2,-1,0,1,2,3\} \cap Z=X \cup Y$, because $X \subset Z$ makes $X \cup Z=Z$.
Both sides equal $\{-3,-2,-1,0,1,2,3\}$, verifying the law.

keyPoints: List letters without repetition
Verify by computing each side separately
Common vowels survive the intersection
modelAnswer:
$X=\{a,e,i\}$ (first three vowels), $Y=\{e,n,r,g,y\}$, $Z=\{a,l,g,e,b,r\}$.
$Y \cup Z=\{a,b,e,g,l,n,r,y\}$, so left side $X \cap(Y \cup Z)=\{a,e\}$.
Right side: $X \cap Y=\{e\}$ and $X \cap Z=\{a,e\}$, whose union is $\{a,e\}$.
Both sides agree, so $X \cap(Y \cup Z)=(X \cap Y) \cup(X \cap Z)$ is verified.
stem:

X = Set of first three Vowels, Y = Set of letters of the word "energy",
Z = Set of letters of the word "algebra"

topicTitle: 3.2 Verification of Associative Laws Using Venn Diagram

modelAnswer:

keyPoints: Ordered pairs are equal exactly when coordinates match in order

modelAnswer:
Equate corresponding coordinates.
(i) $a=7$, $-b=1$ so $b=-1$.
(ii) $2a=-10$ gives $a=-5$; $2b+3=-b$ gives $b=-1$.
(iii) $2a-4=8$ gives $a=6$; $-b+1=6$ gives $b=-5$.
(iv) $y-3=5$ gives $y=8$; $x+2(8)=2$ gives $x=-14$.
(v) From $y-3x=2$, $y=2+3x$; then $2x-(2+3x)=4$ gives $x=-6$, $y=-16$.
(vi) $x=12y-3$; then $4(12y-3)+6y=6$ gives $54y=18$, $y=\frac{1}{3}$, $x=1$.
(vii) Adding $5x+y=6$ and $-x+y=1$ after eliminating: from the second $y=x+1$; then $6x+1=6$ gives $x=\frac{5}{6}$, $y=\frac{11}{6}$.

stem: In the Venn diagram, region A∩B∩C represents elements in:
Given relation R is a subset of ____; if X={2,4,6}, Y={1,3,5}, R={(1,2),(3,4),(5,6)}.
For A={a,b}, B={1,2}, R={(a,1),(b,2)} is a subset of:

1. Encircle the correct option.
i. Set builder form of A - B is:
(a) $\{x \mid x \in \mathrm{~A}\}$
(b) $\{x \mid x \in \mathrm{~A} \wedge x \notin \mathrm{~B}\}$
(c) $\{x \mid x \in \mathrm{~A} \wedge x \in \mathrm{~B}\}$
(d) $\{x \mid x \in \mathrm{~B}\}$
ii. If $\mathrm{A} \cup \mathrm{B}=\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathrm{A} \cap \mathrm{B}=\mathrm{B}$, then:
(a) $\mathrm{A} \subset \mathrm{B}$
(b) $\mathrm{A} \nsupseteq \mathrm{B}$
(c) $\mathrm{A} \supseteq \mathrm{B}$
(d) A $\neq B$
iii. If $\mathrm{A} \subset \mathrm{B}$ then $\mathrm{A}-\mathrm{B}=$
(a) A
(b) B
(c) $\phi$
(d) $\mathrm{B}-\mathrm{A}$
iv. If $\mathrm{A}-\mathrm{B}=\mathrm{B}-\mathrm{A}=\phi$, then:
(a) $\mathrm{A}=\mathrm{B}$
(b) $B \subseteq A$
(c) $\mathrm{A} \subseteq \mathrm{B}$
(d) all a, b \& c
v. Set of common elements of A and $\mathrm{A}^{\mathrm{c}}$ is $\_\_\_\_$ set.
(a) infinite
(b) null
(c) universal
(d) singleton
vi. Set of real numbers can be written in:
(a) tabular form.
(b) descriptive form.
(c) set builder form.
(d) both b and c .
vii. If $\mathrm{R}=\{(2,1),(4,3),(2,2)\}$, then Dom $\mathrm{R}=$
(a) $\{2,4,2\}$
(b) $\{2,4\}$
(c) $\{1,3,2\}$
(d) none of these
viii. If $\mathrm{R}=\{(\mathrm{a}, \mathrm{b}) / \mathrm{a}, \mathrm{b} \in \mathrm{Z} \wedge \mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b}=0\}$, then:
(a) Dom $\mathrm{R} \subset$ Range R
(b) Range $\mathrm{R} \subset \operatorname{Dom} \mathrm{R}$
(c) Dom $\mathrm{R}=$ Range R
(d) none of these.
ix. If $\mathrm{R}=\{(\mathrm{a}, \mathrm{b}) / \mathrm{a}, \mathrm{b} \in \mathrm{N} \wedge \mathrm{a} \times \mathrm{b}=12\}$ then tabular form of R is:
(a) $\{(1,12),(2,6),(3,4),(4,3),(6,2),(12,1)\}$
(b) $\{(1,12),(2,6),(3,4)\}$
(c) $\{(12,1),(6,2),(4,3)\}$
(d) $\{(1,12),(4,3),(2,6)\}$
x. If $\mathrm{n}(\mathrm{A})=\mathrm{p}$, then $\mathrm{n}(\mathrm{A} \times \mathrm{A})=$
(a) p
(b) 2 p
(c) $2 \mathrm{p}^{2}$
(d) $\mathrm{p}^{2}$
xi. If $\mathrm{n}(\mathrm{B})=\mathrm{t}$, then number of binary relations in $\mathrm{B} \times \mathrm{B}$ is:
(a) t
(b) $\mathrm{t}^{2}$
(c) $2^{\mathrm{t}}$
(d) $2^{1^{2}}$
2. If $\mathrm{R}=\{\mathrm{a}, \mathrm{f}, \mathrm{h}, \mathrm{s}\}$ and $\mathrm{S}=\{\mathrm{b}, \mathrm{c}, \mathrm{j}, \mathrm{n}\}$, then

(i) Find the number of binary relations in $\mathrm{R} \times \mathrm{S}$.
(ii) Write any 3 binary relations from $\mathrm{R} \times \mathrm{S}$.
(iii) Write a binary relation whose domain is equal to set R .
(iv) Write a binary relation whose range is equal to set S .
(v) Write a binary relation whose domain is equal to set R and range is equal to set S .

3. Shade $A \cup(B \cap C), A \cap(B \cup C), A-(B \cap C)$ and $B-(A \cup C)$, in the following Venn diagram.
![](./images/586322db-47a5-4f90-b0af-149cd93fd880-068_344_496_438_477.jpg)
4. Verify associative properties of union and intersection through Venn diagram for $\mathrm{X}=\{2 x \mid x \in N \wedge x<20\}, \mathrm{Y}=$ Set of first 6 natural multiples of $3, \mathrm{Z}=\{6 x \mid x \in \mathrm{~W} \wedge x<20\}$
5. Verify distributive law of union over intersection through Venn diagram for the following sets.
$$
\mathrm{A}=\{1,2,3, \ldots\}, \quad \mathrm{B}=\{-1,-2,-3, \ldots\}, \quad \mathrm{C}=\{0, \pm 1, \pm 2, \pm 3, \ldots\}
$$
6. Verify distributive law of intersection over union through Venn diagram for the following sets.
$$
P=\{a, b, c, d, e\}, \quad Q=\{c, d, e, f\}, \quad R=\{g, h, i, j, k\}
$$
7. Create a Venn diagram to illustrate the following information regrading the subsets A and B in the universal set.
    (i) $n(A)=60, n(B)=48, n(A \cap B)=20, n(U)=90$
    (ii) $\mathrm{n}(\mathrm{A})=34, \mathrm{n}(\mathrm{B})=52, \mathrm{n}(\mathrm{A} \cup \mathrm{B})=60, \mathrm{n}(\mathrm{U})=85$
8. 10 boys participated in a Qiraat competition. Among them, Haani, Zubair and Haider recited in Naafi Qiraat style, Abdullah, Umer, Bilal and Ali recited in Al-Kissai Qiraat style while Hassan, Jaffer and Usman recited in Al-Kufi Qiraat style. Represent boys participated in Naafi, Al-Kissai and Al-Kufi styles by sets A, B and C respectively. Find:
    (i) Find tabular form of A, B and C.
    (ii) Draw Venn diagram of situation.
    (iii) Find $A \cap(B \cap C)^{c},(A \cup B) \cap C^{c}, A-(B \cap C)$ and $A-(A \cup B)$.
9. 100 candidates were appeared in an examination. Out of which 45 candidates passed in Mathematics, 40 in Science and 50 in Health. If 12 were passed in Mathematics and Science, 15 in Science and Health, 20 in Health and Mathematics and 5 were passed in all three subjects.
    (i) Illustrate the above information by drawing a Venn diagram.
    (ii) How many candidates were passed at least one subject?
    (iii) How many candidates did not pass any subject?
